# Product Owner Flow Templates

Copy/apply patterns for Product Owner Flow Mode models.

**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, with `references/flow-mode.md` whenever Flow intent is selected
**Purpose:** Provides the user-flow patterns, the provenance table every diagram type keeps and the reply shape every type delivers
**Scope:** Five user-flow patterns, the intake questions, the provenance table and the reply shape. The other types keep their patterns in `assets/templates/`
**Output Path:** None. The model is working data and the board is the deliverable

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Every pattern below passes `scripts/flow_check.py` as a user flow, and `scripts/compose_board.py` composes it into a board. Start from the pattern closest to the flow, rename the nodes after the real screens and triggers, add the board lines below and run the check before the write gate. A process, an architecture, a sequence, a state diagram, an ER diagram or a gantt chart starts from its own file in `assets/templates/`, and keeps the provenance table and the reply shape below.

### Usage

- Node ids are short, stable and camelCase, because the provenance table names them, the composer names every layer after them and the generated fallback mis-routes an underscore
- A label names the screen or the action a person takes, in the words the product uses, in one to four words where those words allow
- A label with a parenthesis, a colon or a slash goes in double quotes, such as `pick["Pick a plan (monthly)"]`
- A decision label is a question, and each exit label is one of its answers
- Every connector is a solid arrow `-->`
- A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes a pink outline, and a styled step is drawn light pink. `style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575` makes that end the goal and the light red pair makes an end a failure. Every pair comes from `references/style-guide.md`, and any other colour is refused or counts as a second accent
- Write `flowchart LR` unless the chain is short, because a board reads wider than it reads tall

### Board lines

The board's own text rides on `%%` comment lines, which the check ignores and the composer reads. Each one is optional, and the generated fallback strips them all:

```text
%% title: Start a return
%% subtitle: How a customer starts a return in the app, from the order list to a confirmed return
%% source: Sources: five app screenshots and the returns doc. Left out: free pickup over 100 euros, a proposal.
%% zone: Find the order: orders, detail
%% zone: Request the return: window, reason, method
```

- `%% title:` names the board. With none, the composer takes a Mermaid frontmatter title, a sequence or gantt `title` line, then `Diagram <n>`
- `%% subtitle:` is one sentence under the title on who reads the board and why
- `%% source:` is the line under the key naming the sources and what was left out
- `%% zone: <label>: <id>, <id>` groups nodes in a tinted section. A user flow or a process without lanes reads its zones in flow order, and once a flow has zones every node sits in exactly one. An ER diagram draws each zone around its entities. Lanes and composite states are zones already, so a laned process, an architecture or a state diagram takes no zone line

---

## 2. PATTERNS

### Linear flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Fill in the form]
    step1 --> step2[Submit]
    step2 --> done([Confirmation shown])
    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
```

### One decision

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Submit the form]
    step1 --> valid{Valid?}
    valid -->|Yes| done([Confirmation shown])
    valid -->|No| fix[Show the field errors]
    fix --> step1
    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
```

### Platform split with a merge dot

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Open the page]) --> open[Open the selector]
    open --> device{Which device?}
    device -->|Desktop| menu[Dropdown menu]
    device -->|Mobile| sheet[Bottom sheet]
    menu --> merge((.))
    sheet --> merge
    merge --> pick[Pick an item]
    pick --> done([Item shown])
    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
```

### Three outcomes

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start([Request sent]) --> result{Response?}
    result -->|Approved| done([Access granted])
    result -->|Rejected| reject([Reason shown])
    result -->|Needs info| ask[Ask for missing info]
    ask --> start
    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
```

### A flow split across

... [2206 characters truncated] ...

ched by joining two sources. Confidence is not the Brief's status, which says whether a row was captured, so the two sit on one item without repeating each other. The rung is the step of the inference ladder in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 that produced the row, and it reads `stated` when a source states the item outright.

A `medium` or `low` row carries its uncertainty in the node label or is left out, so the board never shows a confident shape over a thin source. A board has no marker to hide, so the label is where the uncertainty lives.

Where a frame name and the frame's visible heading differ, both are recorded in the row and the heading labels the node, because the heading is what the reader sees. The difference is a finding for the playback and is never resolved in the row.

Below the table, list every source item that is in no diagram, each with its reason. This is the fidelity ledger sk-design-diagram asks for, so a split or a cut at a lower detail level is named here too:

```text
Left out: <source item>, <reason, such as retired material, a split that ends before it or a cut at the simplified detail level>
```

---

## 4. REPLY SHAPE

```text
<board URL>
Read-back: <counts the type's reference names, each as n of n>
Extensions: <n> of <n> pins, <n> of <n> legend stickies, <n> overlaps
Left out: <source item>, <reason>
Finding: <a read-back finding, a write warning, an open item or a question>
HVR self-scan: <n> hard blockers. Fixed: <terms>. Kept with reason: <terms>.
```

The `Read-back:` counts follow the type: nodes, connectors and labelled decision exits for a user flow, lanes as well for a process, participants and messages for a sequence, states and transitions for a state diagram, entities, relationships and attributes for an ER diagram, and sections, tasks and milestones for a gantt chart. The `Extensions:` line appears only when the write added any, and the `Left out:` line only when the provenance table lists items left out, so the user sees what the board does not hold. When only a screenshot could be read, the read-back line ends with `, read visually`, because a picture cannot prove which nodes a connector joins. When the connector has no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done.

These lines are the whole reply, and the self-scan is always the last. Each finding, warning, open item or question is one `Finding:` line, and nothing follows the self-scan. The playback of the settled rows runs before the model and the gate, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 8 sets out, and it never becomes a line here.

---

## 5. INTAKE QUESTIONS

The type table in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 reads as questions. Ask them as an interview before the model is written, in three rounds that depend on each other, because an answer in one round settles what the next round may ask.

| Round | Asks | Settles |
|---|---|---|
| One | The reader, the question and the outcome | Who the board is for, what it must answer and what the reader decides next |
| Two | Entry, exit and actors | Where the flow starts, where it ends and who takes each step |
| Three | Decisions, states, sources and class | Where the flow branches, which states exist, which source states each fact and what class that source holds |

### Every question carries a reading and a recommendation

A user who does not know an answer should still be able to accept one, so every question is put in this shape:

```text
Reading: <what the sources already show for this question>
Question: <the one thing still open>
Recommended: <the answer the AI would take>
Why: <the one line of reason>
```

- One to three questions per round and no later round while an earlier one is open
- Never a question a supplied source already answers, because that answer is stated as the reading instead
- A round closes when each of its questions is answered, accepted or corrected

### A vague answer is asked again

An answer that names nothing is asked once more with one probe from this set, and never with the same wording twice:

- A concrete scenario, such as one example walked from the first click to the end
- An edge case, such as two of these arriving at once
- A contradiction, such as one source stating this and another stating the opposite
- A term, such as what one word means in this product
- A scale, such as how many of these exist on a busy day
- A failure mode, such as what the reader sees when one step fails
- A boundary, such as where this flow stops and another one begins

### An unanswered question is never a dead end

When the user skips a question or says they do not know, the AI takes the recommended answer. That fact is marked assumed in the Brief and named in the playback before the gate, so the user corrects it before anything is written. A row the user corrects is recorded as `corrected` and counts as settled. No later round asks it again.

---
title: "FigJam Type - User Flow"
description: "A person's path through a product composed as a FigJam board: four shapes, labelled exits, colour by kind, optional zones and a nine-node budget."
contextType: implementation
importance_tier: important
trigger_phrases:
  - "figjam user flow"
  - "user flow rules"
  - "screen flow figjam"
  - "merge dot"
version: 1.0.2.0
---

# FigJam Type - User Flow

A user flow is the screens and choices one person passes through to reach a goal. It is the default Flow type and the strictest, because it is drawn from screenshots and frames a reader will compare node by node.

**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, when the Flow route draws a user flow
**Purpose:** The grammar, rules, budget and read-back for a user flow
**Pairs With:** `assets/flow-templates.md`

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

**The reader's question:** which screens does a person pass through, and where do they choose?

- A flow drawn from screenshots, from Figma frames or from a product doc that walks one person through the product
- A platform split, such as desktop and mobile, that rejoins on a later screen
- A journey, which Flow Mode does not draw as such, redrawn as the screens it visits

Use another type when several people or teams hand work to each other (a process), when the subject is services and stores (an architecture) or when time order between systems is the point (a sequence).

---

## 2. WHAT THE BOARD DRAWS

`flowchart LR` or `flowchart TD`, composed into a board as Section 6 sets out. No `%% type:` line is needed, because a flowchart with none is a user flow.

| Shape | Mermaid | Means |
|---|---|---|
| Stadium | `id([Label])` | The flow starts or ends here |
| Rectangle | `id[Label]` | A screen or an action |
| Rhombus | `id{Label?}` | A choice, written as a question |
| Circle | `id((.))` | A merge dot, where branches rejoin, with no words |

Every connector is a solid one-way arrow, `-->`, with an optional label: `a -->|Yes| b`.

On the board the first screen takes the `entry` role, every other screen the `neutral` role, a decision a diamond in the `decision` role, the goal the `goal` role and every other end the `exit` role, beside the main line rather than on it, and `assets/figjam-design.md` names the swatch each role draws. The main route from the first screen to the goal runs on one straight line, and `%% zone:` lines group the screens into named stages, as `assets/flow-templates.md` Section 1 sets out.

Every move carries an actor in the model, one of a person, a system or a timer. A system step is marked automatic and a timer step is fired by time, so neither is ever counted as a missing user action.

---

## 3. RULES

The check enforces:

- **Four shapes only.** No other shape, no subgraph and never a colour per type. A `%% zone:` line does the grouping instead
- **A decision has 1 to 3 exits, each labelled.** A fourth outcome means the decision is two decisions
- **Every node connected, every step with a way in and a way out.** Only a stadium starts or ends the flow, and a stadium never sits mid-flow. The first node may take a loop back to it
- **A merge dot carries no words**
- **Solid one-way arrows only.** A dotted, thick, headless or two-way connector would carry a second meaning. A proposal's status goes in its label, and a `style` line marks the goal
- **Left to right or top to bottom,** the same way for every diagram of one flow. Left to right is the default, because the composer keeps the main route on one straight line across a board that reads wider than tall and sets each branch beside it. Top to bottom suits a short flow
- **Labels of at most 40 characters on one line,** in double quotes when they hold a parenthesis, a colon or a slash
- **camelCase ids,** never an underscore or a reserved word such as `end`
- **No emoji, markup or literal `\n`** anywhere in the block but a `%%` comment
- **At most 9 nodes,** and exactly one `style` line from `references/style-guide.md`

Judged by hand:

- **Labels name the screen or the action in the product's own words,** one to four words where those words allow
- **A decision label is a question and each exit one of its answers**
- **Exits read the same way across the flow,** such as Yes to the right and No below, so a reader learns the pattern once
- **The shape carries the type, so the label does not repeat it.** Write `valid{Card valid?}`, never `valid{Decision: card valid?}`
- **A state is a screen in another condition, and no fifth shape carries it.** A state earns its own node only when a different action reaches it or a reader can be trapped in it, and otherwise the condition goes in the screen's label and under `Left out:`

---

## 4. BUDGET AND SPLITTING

Nine nodes is sk-design-diagram's general budget and matches what a hand-drawn user flow uses. A longer flow splits into diagrams that hand off through a named end and a start with the same label, all in one file. Every source step lands in one diagram or under `Left out:`, never dropped silently. At `Meeting screen` distance labels drop to 32 characters. At `Wall` distance the budget drops to 6 nodes, with labels at 25 characters, as the reading distance dial in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out.

---

## 5. COLOUR, ZONES AND NOTES

The composer colours every screen by its kind. A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes the accent's outline. A styled step is drawn in the accent's pair. The line marks meaning: on an end it makes that end the goal, or with the light red pair a failure, and on a screen it puts that screen in focus, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out. Zones are `%% zone:` lines in flow order, and once a flow has zones every screen sits in one. A note on a screen, such as a drop-off rate, goes on through the pins and legend recipe in `references/hybrid-workflow.md`.

---

## 6. WRITING THE BOARD

`scripts/compose_board.py` composes the model and one `use_figma` call draws the board, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 6 sets out. On the generated fallback, `generate_diagram` takes `name`, `mermaidSyntax` and `userIntent`, with `name` set to the flow and its hand-off and no `useArchitectureLayoutCode`. The `fj` route can also draw a user flow when neither hosted tool is connected.

---

## 7. READ-BACK

Count on the board, against the model: nodes, connectors, decision exits labelled, every node label, and for each model connector a board connector joining the same two nodes in the same direction with the same label, following a routed edge through its legs as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 7 sets out. When the flow has zones, each screen sits in its zone.

```text
Read-back: 8 of 8 nodes, 8 of 8 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled
```

---

## 8. PATTERNS AND EXAMPLE

- `assets/flow-templates.md` holds five user-flow patterns that pass the check
- `assets/examples/user-flow-fernhouse-return.md` walks one flow from screenshots to the reply

On the board the first screen takes the `entry` role, every other screen the `neutral` role, a decision a diamond in the `decision` role, the goal the `goal` role and every other end the `exit` role, beside the main line rather than on it, and `assets/figjam-design.md` names the swatch each role draws. The main route from the first screen to the goal runs on one straight line, and `%% zone:` lines group the screens into named stages, as `assets/flow-templates.md` Section 1 sets out.

Every move carries an actor in the model, one of a person, a system or a timer. A system step is marked automatic and a timer step is fired by time, so neither is ever counted as a missing user action.

---

## 3. RULES

The check enforces:

- **Four shapes only.** No other shape, no subgraph and never a colour per type. A `%% zone:` line does the grouping instead
- **A decision has 1 to 3 exits, each labelled.** A fourth outcome means the decision is two decisions
- **Every node connected, every step with a way in and a way out.** Only a stadium starts or ends the flow, and a stadium never sits mid-flow. The first node may take a loop back to it
- **A merge dot carries no words**
- **Solid one-way arrows only.** A dotted, thick, headless or two-way connector would carry a second meaning. A proposal's status goes in its label, and a `style` line marks the goal
- **Left to right or top to bottom,** the same way for every diagram of one flow. Left to right is the default, because the composer keeps the main route on one straight line across a board that reads wider than tall and sets each branch beside it. Top to bottom suits a short flow
- **Labels of at most 40 characters on one line,** in double quotes when they hold a parenthesis, a colon or a slash
- **camelCase ids,** never an underscore or a reserved word such as `end`
- **No emoji, markup or literal `\n`** anywhere in the block but a `%%` comment
- **At most 9 nodes,** and exactly one `style` line from `references/style-guide.md`

Judged by hand:

- **Labels name the screen or the action in the product's own words,** one to four words where those words allow
- **A decision label is a question and each exit one of its answers**
- **Exits read the same way across the flow,** such as Yes to the right and No below, so a reader learns the pattern once
- **The shape carries the type, so the label does not repeat it.** Write `valid{Card valid?}`, never `valid{Decision: card valid?}`
- **A state is a screen in another condition, and no fifth shape carries it.** A state earns its own node only when a different action reaches it or a reader can be trapped in it, and otherwise the condition goes in the screen's label and under `Left out:`

---

## 4. BUDGET AND SPLITTING

Nine nodes is sk-design-diagram's general budget and matches what a hand-drawn user flow uses. A longer flow splits into diagrams that hand off through a named end and a start with the same label, all in one file. Every source step lands in one diagram or under `Left out:`, never dropped silently. At `Meeting screen` distance labels drop to 32 characters. At `Wall` distance the budget drops to 6 nodes, with labels at 25 characters, as the reading distance dial in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out.

---

## 5. COLOUR, ZONES AND NOTES

The composer colours every screen by its kind. A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes the accent's outline. A styled step is drawn in the accent's pair. The line marks meaning: on an end it makes that end the goal, or with the light red pair a failure, and on a screen it puts that screen in focus, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out. Zones are `%% zone:` lines in flow order, and once a flow has zones every screen sits in one. A note on a screen, such as a drop-off rate, goes on through the pins and legend recipe in `references/hybrid-workflow.md`.

---

## 6. WRITING THE BOARD

`scripts/compose_board.py` composes the model and one `use_figma` call draws the board, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 6 sets out. On the generated fallback, `generate_diagram` takes `name`, `mermaidSyntax` and `userIntent`, with `name` set to the flow and its hand-off and no `useArchitectureLayoutCode`. The `fj` route can also draw a user flow when neither hosted tool is connected.

---

## 7. READ-BACK

Count on the board, against the model: nodes, connectors, decision exits labelled, every node label, and for each model connector a board connector joining the same two nodes in the same direction with the same label, following a routed edge through its legs as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 7 sets out. When the flow has zones, each screen sits in its zone.

```text
Read-back: 8 of 8 nodes, 8 of 8 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled
```

---

## 8. PATTERNS AND EXAMPLE

- `assets/flow-templates.md` holds five user-flow patterns that pass the check
- `assets/examples/user-flow-fernhouse-return.md` walks one flow from screenshots to the reply
